items.name: open-orange
items.description: Run Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects unchanged on AWS, GCP, Azure or your own servers.
items.readme:
Run Cloudflare Workers anywhere: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or your own servers.

The same developer experience, without the runtime limits, for a fraction of the bill.

Docs · Deploy · Migrate · Bindings · Examples · Discord

## What is OpenOrange OpenOrange runs your existing Cloudflare Workers project on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or your own servers, with no changes to your code. It's built with four goals: - **Zero refactoring, zero-downtime migration**: your Workers and Durable Objects run as they are, and your data moves off Cloudflare while your app keeps serving. - **The same developer experience**: `wrangler dev` becomes `orange dev`, and everything underneath is open source and self-hostable. - **Simpler bills**: you pay for the machines you run on, not Cloudflare's metering or an enterprise contract. Compute is 4.8× cheaper and storage 8.7× cheaper. - **Built for scale**: storage is backed by S3, so scaling out is a matter of adding machines. ## Quickstart You need a Worker project with a `wrangler.jsonc`, `wrangler.json`, or `wrangler.toml` (or use [`examples/hello-durable-object`](examples/hello-durable-object)), Node.js 22 or later, and pnpm. Deploying also needs Docker. ### Use a coding agent Paste this into your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) from your Worker project: ```text First, add the Rivet MCP (https://mcp.rivet.dev/mcp) to this agent, and ask me to approve the Rivet sign-in. Then run this project's Cloudflare Worker on Rivet with OpenOrange: ask me where it should run (on my machine, on a Rivet cluster, or on my own Rivet Engine), read https://github.com/rivet-dev/open-orange/blob/main/README.md and follow its quickstart. Do not change my app code. ``` ### Step 1: Install Install the `orange` CLI globally, then run it in your Worker project. Your code and your Wrangler configuration do not change. ```sh pnpm add -g open-orange ``` ### Step 2: Run your Worker Your Worker answers on `http://localhost:8787`. Each Durable Object runs as a Rivet Actor with its own SQLite database, kept in `.open-orange/`. ```sh $ orange dev Binding Resource Runs on env.COUNTER Durable Object Rivet Actor · Counter ● Ready in 4.6s Local http://127.0.0.1:8787 ``` ### Step 3: Deploy `orange deploy` builds an image of your Worker and rolls it out to a Rivet cluster, then prints its public URL. ```sh $ orange login $ orange link --cluster $ orange deploy ✓ Deployed my-worker URL https://api.example.com ``` See the [deploy guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/deploy/), or [self-host it](#self-host). ## Migrate your data without downtime `orange migrate` moves your Durable Objects off Cloudflare with zero downtime.

See the [migration guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/migrate/) for every step, rollback, and what cannot move. ## Run it where you want Next to your database, in the cloud and region you choose. - **Rivet Cloud**, fully managed: a dedicated cluster on AWS or Google Cloud, in the region you choose. Operated by Rivet. - **BYOC**, your cloud and our ops: your AWS, Google Cloud or Azure account. Operated by Rivet over an outbound connection. - **Self-hosted**, open source under Apache 2.0: any cloud, Hetzner, on-prem or air-gapped. Operated by you. ### Self-host 1. **Build the Docker image.** `orange deploy --dry-run` writes the build and calls no API. Push the image to a registry your servers can pull from. ```sh orange deploy --dry-run --outdir out docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f out/Dockerfile -t my-worker out/context ``` 2. **Run the Rivet control plane.** Follow Rivet's guide for your platform: [Kubernetes](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/kubernetes/), [AWS ECS](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/aws-ecs/), [Docker Compose](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/docker-compose/), [Hetzner](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/hetzner/), [Railway](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/railway/), [Render](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/render/), [a VM](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/vm/). 3. **Run your image as worker nodes.** Point each container at the control plane with `RIVET_ENDPOINT`, following Rivet's guide for your platform: [Kubernetes](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/kubernetes/), [AWS ECS](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/aws-ecs/), [Docker Compose](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/docker-compose/), [Hetzner](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/hetzner/), [Railway](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/railway/), [Render](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/render/), [a VM](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/vm/). See [self-hosting](https://openorange.dev/docs/deploy/#self-host) in the deploy guide. ## How pricing compares Cloudflare's meters, priced on raw AWS: Graviton EC2 in us-east-1 with 40% headroom, and S3 in your account. See [the cost model](https://openorange.dev/#cost). | | Cloudflare | OpenOrange | | |---|---|---|---| | Durable Object compute | $0.045 per GB-hour | $0.0094 per GB-hour | 4.8× cheaper | | Durable Object storage | $0.20 per GB-month | $0.023 per GB-month | 8.7× cheaper | | SQLite writes | $1.00 per million rows | about $0.18 per million | 5.7× cheaper | ## No runtime limits 128 MB is all the memory a Cloudflare Worker gets. OpenOrange runs your Workers and Durable Objects on machines you choose, so the limits are your hardware's. | Limit | Cloudflare Workers Paid | OpenOrange | |---|---|---| | Memory per Worker or Durable Object | 128 MB | Up to your machine's memory. The Node.js heap is up to about 4 GB by default, and configurable. | | CPU time per request | 30 s default, 5 min max | No cap | | Cron, queue and alarm handlers | 15 min wall time | No cap | | Open connections per request | 6 at once | OS limits | | Storage per Durable Object | 10 GB | No cap | | Worker bundle | 64 MiB | No cap | | Node.js | `nodejs_compat` subset | Stock Node.js | ## Architecture

- **Your containers** run your Workers and Durable Objects, in any cloud or on your own servers. - **Rivet** places each Durable Object on a container and routes requests to it. - **S3** stores each object's SQLite data. See [Architecture](https://openorange.dev/docs/architecture/). ## Supported bindings | Cloudflare binding | Status | Runs on | |---|---|---| | [Durable Objects](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/durable-objects/) | Partial | One Rivet Actor for each object, with its own SQLite database | | [KV](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/kv/), [D1](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/d1/), [Rate Limiting](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/rate-limiting/) | Drop-in | Rivet Actors | | [Cache](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/cache/) | Partial | One Rivet Actor for each cache name | | [Queues](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/queues/) | Drop-in | One Rivet Actor for each queue | | [Workflows](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/workflows/) | Partial | Cloudflare's own Workflows engine, with one Rivet Actor for each instance | | [Cron Triggers](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/cron-triggers/) | Drop-in | A Rivet Actor | | [Tail Workers](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/tail-workers/) | Partial | Rivet Durable Streams | | [R2](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/r2/) | Pluggable | A Rivet Actor, or Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Cloudflare R2 or MinIO | | [Worker Loader](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/worker-loader/) | Partial | A separate process in an agentOS VM | | [Workers AI](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/workers-ai/) | Pluggable | OpenRouter, OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint | | [Send Email](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/email/) | Pluggable | Amazon SES, or any SMTP server | | [Browser Rendering](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/browser-rendering/) | Pluggable | Browserbase, or any Chrome DevTools endpoint | | [Hyperdrive](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/hyperdrive/) | Drop-in | Your Postgres or MySQL database, with a direct connection | | [Sandbox](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/sandbox/) | Pluggable | E2B, Daytona, Freestyle, agentOS, or a local directory | | Analytics Engine | Not supported | `writeDataPoint()` drops each data point | | Vectorize, Images, Media, Stream, Pipelines, AI Search, mTLS certificates, VPC, and legacy blobs | Not supported | Calls throw | **Drop-in** runs as on Cloudflare. **Pluggable** runs on a provider you configure. **Partial** runs with known differences, listed on each binding's page. See [binding configuration](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/configuration/) for every Wrangler key and the variables each provider needs, and [Compatibility](https://openorange.dev/docs/compatibility/) for the test results. ## Questions
Wait, wasn't Cloudflare supposed to be cheaper? For small, spiky Workers, it often is: the free tier and per-request pricing are hard to beat. The meters add up once Durable Objects stay busy. The same GB-hours on Graviton EC2 cost about a fifth as much, and writes cost a fraction of that.
Is OpenOrange a fork of Cloudflare? No. OpenOrange implements the Workers API on Node.js and maps each Cloudflare service onto Rivet. It uses Wrangler to read your configuration, and it reuses some MIT-licensed Cloudflare code, such as the Workflows engine. It does not run workerd.
Why not just run workerd directly? workerd is Cloudflare's runtime, not its platform. KV, D1, R2, Queues, Workflows and the Cache API are bindings that call services you have to build, and Durable Objects keep their data on one machine with nothing to place, replicate or scale them. See [OpenOrange vs workerd](https://openorange.dev/vs-workerd/).
Do I need to learn Rivet? No. Rivet is the control plane underneath. You use the `orange` CLI and your Wrangler configuration.
What does it cost? OpenOrange is Apache 2.0 and free. Self-host Rivet and your cloud bill is the only bill. Rivet Cloud and BYOC pricing is at [rivet.dev/pricing](https://rivet.dev/pricing).
What happens to the data already in KV, Durable Objects and R2? `orange migrate` moves Durable Objects while your app serves, with no downtime. D1 databases are interrupted for a few minutes while they copy. R2 is S3-compatible, so `rclone` or `aws s3 sync` moves buckets.
Does it run at the edge? It runs wherever you deploy it, in as many regions as you want. Most backends talk to one database, and running next to it is faster than running at the edge.
Who maintains OpenOrange? [Rivet](https://rivet.dev). OpenOrange is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cloudflare, Inc.
## Compare - [OpenOrange vs Cloudflare Durable Objects](https://openorange.dev/vs-durable-objects/): limits, latency, residency, and moving off. - [OpenOrange vs workerd](https://openorange.dev/vs-workerd/): a runtime for one Worker, versus your whole app in production. - [OpenOrange vs celld](https://openorange.dev/vs-celld/): runtime limits, live migration, integrations, and support. - [OpenOrange vs Rivet](https://openorange.dev/vs-rivet/): when to use Rivet directly, and how to combine them. - [OpenOrange vs Miniflare](https://openorange.dev/vs-miniflare/): a local simulator, versus production. ## Resources - [Deploy guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/deploy/): Rivet Cloud, self-hosting, variables, secrets, and rollback. - [Migration guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/migrate/): how to cut over, how to roll back, and what cannot move. - [Bindings](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/): one page for each binding and runtime API, with its known differences. - [Architecture](https://openorange.dev/docs/architecture/): how OpenOrange runs your Worker on Rivet. - [Examples](examples/): Workers that you can copy, with no OpenOrange imports. - [Real projects](packages/cloudflare-conformance/real-projects): open-source Workers run through `orange dev`, with what works and what does not. - [Discord](https://rivet.dev/discord): questions and support. ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)

items.name: super-odyssey-pc-recomp
items.description: A native Windows PC port of Super Mario Odyssey by static recompilation. Bring your own game: no game files included.
items.readme:
A native Windows PC port of Super Mario Odyssey, made by static recompilation - from your own copy of the game.

> [!IMPORTANT] > **You must bring your own game.** This project contains **no game files, no game code, no assets and no keys** - > only the installer and the source code. To play, you need the **`exefs` and `romfs` folders of your own copy of > Super Mario Odyssey**, already extracted. No keys are needed or asked for. Instructions for getting game files are > not provided, and requests for game files or keys will be closed. > [!WARNING] > **This is an early preview.** The whole game can be played, but there are known issues (see > [Known issues](#known-issues)) and things that still need fixing. Please report what you find. ## What it is The game's ARM64 code is translated to C ahead of time and compiled into a regular Windows program - no emulator runs while you play. The parts of the Switch the game talks to (kernel, system services, the NVN graphics API, audio) are reimplemented on the PC, with Vulkan for graphics. - **Installer** that takes your game's extracted `exefs` and `romfs` folders (1.0.0, or 1.4.1 with the update applied) - **Every shader compiled at install time**, so effects don't stutter the first time they appear - **Up to 4x internal resolution**, NVIDIA **DLSS / DLAA**, AMD FSR 1, SMAA, ultrawide *Fill window* - **Native 120 FPS** (experimental) or frame interpolation, anisotropic filtering, smooth gradients - Keyboard and controller rebinding, RomFS mods, an in-game settings menu, and **built-in updates** from this page Windows 10 / 11 (x64) only for now. ## Install 1. Download the latest `...-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases) and extract it anywhere you own (for example `D:\Games`, **not** Program Files). Start `SuperOdysseyRecomp.exe`. It isn't code-signed: if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*. 2. The installer asks for: 1. **Your game**: the folder that holds the extracted **`exefs`** and **`romfs`** folders of your own Super Mario Odyssey - version **1.0.0**, or **1.4.1** with the update already applied (its full `romfs`, not only the update's). `exefs` holds `main`, `main.npdm` and `sdk`; `romfs` holds folders such as `StageData` and `SystemData`. 2. **Install the game to**: where the game data, saves and shaders go (about 12 GB). 3. Press **Install**. It copies the game data, recompiles the game code for your PC (a few minutes) and compiles every shader (several minutes, once). 4. Press **Play**. The game opens in fullscreen; later starts go straight to the game.

## Updating New versions are published on this page. The game checks for them at start (in the background - only GitHub is contacted and nothing about you or your game is sent; you can switch this off) and shows a note when one is out. Open the menu (**F1**) > **Updates** > **Download and install**, then **Restart now**. Your game files, saves, settings and mods stay; if the new version needs it, the game code is rebuilt and the shaders re-prepared once, by themselves. You can also download the new zip from [Releases](../../releases) and extract it over your current folder. ## Known issues This is a preview. Known problems and things not done yet: - **Version 1.4.1** is newer in this port than 1.0.0 and less tested: native 120 FPS and the frame interpolation's pose smoothing are tuned on 1.0.0, so 1.4.1 can show more jitter or small glitches with them on. - **Native 120 FPS** is experimental on both versions: some objects or effects can move unevenly or look doubled. - **A short stutter can still happen** the first time a rare effect is drawn whose pipeline state nobody has recorded yet. It's prepared then and kept for next time. - **Online features** of the game (anything that needs Nintendo's servers) don't work. - **Code mods** (exefs patches, IPS / pchtxt, online mods) can't be used: the game code is rebuilt from the original. RomFS mods work. - **Windows Defender** may flag the new, unsigned program by its machine-learning guess (a `!ml` detection) - it decrypts a file, builds code and starts helper programs, which looks unusual. Please report it as a false positive at https://www.microsoft.com/wdsi/filesubmission and open an issue with the detection name. - **Windows only.** A CPU with AVX2 and a Vulkan 1.3 GPU are required. - Graphics glitches can show up in places nobody has tested yet - please report them with a screenshot. ## Reporting a problem Open an [issue](../../issues) with: - what happened and where in the game (a screenshot helps), - your game version (1.0.0 or 1.4.1), Windows version, CPU and GPU, - the log, `SuperOdysseyRecomp.log`, from the install folder (it doesn't contain any game files). For a graphics glitch, pressing **F9** where it happens saves the frame's details into the log, which helps a lot. ## What you need - Windows 10 / 11 (x64), a CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer), a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and an up-to-date driver - 8 GB RAM (16 GB recommended), about 12 GB free disk space - The extracted `exefs` and `romfs` folders of your own Super Mario Odyssey (1.0.0, or 1.4.1 with the update applied) ## Settings Open the menu with **F1** or **Esc** (controller: Home / Guide button). Switch tabs with L / R (Q / E); the text on the right explains the selected setting. - **Display**: windowed, borderless or exclusive fullscreen, display resolution, aspect ratio (ultrawide *Fill window*) - **Graphics**: internal resolution, NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA (presets, sharpening), AMD FSR 1, SMAA, anisotropic filtering, smooth gradients - **Performance**: 120 FPS (native or interpolated), shader preloading and warm-up, FPS counter and performance overlay, compile shaders again at the next start - **Audio**: volume, reverb, movie audio, mute in background - **Controls**: language, vibration, stick deadzone, mouse camera (sensitivity, invert), button prompts (keyboard / controller), skip controller tips, key and button rebinding - **Mods**: switch RomFS mods on and off - **Updates**: this version, check / install updates, the project page ## Controls | Switch | Keyboard | Controller | |---|---|---| | Left stick | W A S D | left stick | | Right stick (camera) | mouse, or Num 8 / 4 / 5 / 6 | right stick | | A / B / X / Y | K / J / L / I | by position (east = A, south = B) | | L / R, ZL / ZR | Q / E, 1 / 3 | shoulder buttons / triggers | | + / - | Enter / Backspace | Start / Back | | Stick clicks | F / Num 0 | stick clicks | | D-pad | arrow keys | d-pad | Fullscreen: F11 or Alt+Enter. Everything can be rebound in the menu. The mouse turns the camera while you play: the pointer stays in the window until you open the menu (Esc) or switch to another window. Sensitivity, invert up / down, or switching it off: menu > Controls > Mouse. The game's button icons follow what you play with: after a key press or mouse movement they show the keys you bound (WASD for moving, a mouse for the camera), after a controller press the controller's buttons. Menu > Controls > *Button prompts* can fix them to one or the other. ## Files The program folder holds the program; the install folder (the same one unless you chose another) holds: - `extracted\` - your game data as the installer wrote it and the game code built from it (`odyssey_game.dll`) - `save\` - your saves, `cache\` - compiled shaders, `powermoon.ini` - settings, `SuperOdysseyRecomp.log` - the log - `mods\` - optional RomFS mods, each in its own folder (`mods\\romfs\...`; the Atmosphere layout works too) Never share `extracted\` or anything built from it: it's Nintendo's game. ## Building from source Needs MSYS2 (UCRT64: clang, SDL3, FFmpeg, shaderc, Python) - `tools\setup_windows.ps1` installs them. See [docs/BUILD-windows.md](docs/BUILD-windows.md). 1. Put your extracted game folders into `extracted\` (`extracted\exefs\`, `extracted\romfs\`), or start the built program and let its installer copy them there. 2. From an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell in this folder: make gen # recompile the game from extracted/exefs into generated/ make -j16 # build/SuperOdysseyRecomp.exe and the game code, build/odyssey_game.dll make dlls # copy SDL3 / FFmpeg / shaderc DLLs next to the exe 3. Built with heavy help from AI coding agents, directed and tested by a human. ## Credits - **Power Moon Recomp** by its contributors - the Super Mario Odyssey port this project continues (MIT license); # FFmpeg-GUI-Editor-Windows — Ready-to-Use Free Portable Video Editor (.exe)

**FFmpeg-GUI-Editor-Windows** is a lightweight, fast, and **free open-source video editor for Windows 10 and Windows 11** that works as an intuitive graphical user interface (**FFmpeg GUI**). Built specifically for users who want to **download a ready-to-use `.exe` executable** to trim, crop, compress, and convert videos without touching the command line.

No installation, no Python setup, no manual `PATH` configuration, and no watermarks. Just download the release files, place them in the same folder, and start editing. Licensed under **GPL v3**.

---

### 📥 Direct Download & Important Setup Instructions (`.exe` + `libvlc.dll`)
The release package consists of **two required files**: the main executable (`.exe`) and the media engine library (**`libvlc.dll`**).

1. Open the **[Releases](../../releases)** page of this repository.
2. Download **both files** from the latest release:
   * **`FFmpeg-GUI-Editor.exe`** (the main application)
   * **`libvlc.dll`** (required core video playback & rendering library)
3. **Important:** Place both files inside the **same folder** on your PC or USB drive (do not separate them).
4. Double-click the **`.exe`** file to launch the editor immediately — no installation required.

> **⚠️ Note:** Both the `.exe` file and `libvlc.dll` must remain in the exact same directory for the program to start and preview videos properly.

---

### 🖼️ Interface & Quick Visual Guide
![FFmpeg-GUI-Editor-Windows Visual Guide](blob/main/guide.png)



---

### 🌍 Multi-Language Interface (6 Languages Built-In)
Switch between 6 languages directly in the interface without downloading extra language packs:
* 🇬🇧 **English**

* 🇨🇳 **中文** (Chinese)
* 🇩🇪 **Deutsch** (German)
* 🇫🇷 **Français** (French)
* 🇮🇹 **Italiano** (Italiano)

# Mate

Your mate while you shop.

A shopping agent you text before you shop.
Live product: mate.fm

This repository is the open-source **starter** for Mate: original icons in the mate.fm palette, a small runnable text agent, a web chat demo, docs for GitHub Pages, and clearly labeled demo providers. It is not the production service, and it is not connected to Mate’s live merchant network. --- ## What Mate is From [mate.fm](https://mate.fm/): > Your shopping agent with 200k merchant partnerships. Text Mate before you shop to save. Cashback and codes are offered on request, wherever you shop online. The site lists, among others: Nature INT, NIKE, The New Yorker, Walmart, Dell, Cheerble, SEMrush, Verso, Casper, Slice, Charity: Water, MyFonts. mate.fm marks its illustrated conversations as fictional. Example codes, deliveries and cashback on the marketing site — and every demo reply in this starter — are **not** real offers. Get early access on [mate.fm](https://mate.fm/). Terms and privacy for the live product are published at [joincheckmate.com/terms-conditions](https://joincheckmate.com/terms-conditions) and [joincheckmate.com/privacy-policy](https://joincheckmate.com/privacy-policy). --- ## Features Text Mate before you shop. Here’s what you get back — copied from the product site, with the original icons in this repo.
01 · Cashback when you text first
Text Mate before you buy. It sends you the link that tracks your order, and the cashback lands in your balance.
02 · Discount codes generated for you
Tell Mate where you’re shopping. It gets you a discount code made just for you.
03 · Every package, tracked
A text when it ships and when it’s at your door. Mate can tell your room-mate too.
04 · Price drop alerts
Send Mate something you’re eyeing. It watches the price and texts you the moment it drops.
The starter answers the same kinds of texts with **demo** data, always labeled `[demo]`. --- ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Shopper text
web chat, CLI, or SMS] --> B[Intent parser] B --> C{Intent} C -->|cashback at store| D[Cashback provider] C -->|code for store| E[Codes provider] C -->|track number| F[Tracking stub] C -->|watch url| G[Price watcher] C -->|unknown| H[Optional OpenRouter] D --> I[Reply] E --> I F --> I G --> I H --> I I --> A ``` In production, those providers talk to Mate’s merchant network. In this repo they are **demo implementations**: placeholder links, `DEMO-…` codes, scripted shipment statuses, and a local price-watch job that does not scrape live product pages. An optional OpenRouter LLM fallback (via `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) only runs when the parser does not recognize an intent. No API keys are hardcoded. --- ## Quickstart Python 3.10 or newer. No third-party packages are required at runtime. ```bash git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/mate.git cd mate python -m mate chat "cashback at Demo Shop" python -m mate serve ``` Then open [http://127.0.0.1:8080](http://127.0.0.1:8080). Useful commands: ```bash python -m mate help python -m mate "code for Demo Shop" python -m mate "track DEMO-123456" python -m mate "watch https://shop.example/nimbus-lamp" python -m mate watch --simulate-drop python -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` Docker: ```bash docker build -t mate-starter . docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 mate-starter ``` --- ## Setup and configuration Copy [`.env.example`](.env.example) and export whatever you need. All settings are optional for the local demo. | Variable | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `MATE_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address for `python -m mate serve` | | `MATE_PORT` | `8080` | Port | | `MATE_DATA_DIR` | `data/` | JSON store for demo wallets, packages, watches | | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | unset | Enables LLM fallback for unrecognized messages | | `MATE_MODEL` | `openrouter/auto` | OpenRouter model id | | `MATE_HTTP_REFERER` | `https://mate.fm` | Sent as `HTTP-Referer` to OpenRouter | | `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | unset | Used only if signature checks are on | | `TWILIO_VALIDATE_SIGNATURE` | `0` | Set to `1` to require a valid `X-Twilio-Signature` | Point a Twilio number’s messaging webhook at `POST /webhooks/twilio`. The adapter is a stub: it reads `Body` and `From`, replies with TwiML, and never sends a real SMS by itself. --- ## Repository layout ``` mate/ Python package (agent, server, providers, web chat) tests/ unittest suite docs/ GitHub Pages landing site, in the mate.fm style assets/brand/ Logo, app icon, favicon assets/icons/ 50 original SVG icons + PNG 64/128/512 + preview sheet assets/social-preview.png tools/generate_assets.py ``` The icon catalog, with names, lives in [`assets/icons/README.md`](assets/icons/README.md). Preview: ![Mate icon set](assets/icons/preview.png) --- ## Roadmap - Swap demo providers for live Mate network adapters - Persist shopper sessions beyond the local JSON store - Richer tracking (carrier webhooks) behind the same intent interface - A real price fetcher behind `PriceProvider`, still clearly separated from the demo - iMessage / WhatsApp-style delivery in production stays on mate.fm; this starter keeps SMS and web --- ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Security reports go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Product copy and the public store count above are taken from [mate.fm](https://mate.fm/). The logo mark matches the public mark at `https://mate.fm/icon.svg`. Icons in `assets/icons/` are original. This repo does not include third-party merchant logos.

# Kimi Uncensored — every uncensored and abliterated Kimi model, indexed and tested **An uncensored Kimi model is a Moonshot AI Kimi variant with refusal behavior reduced — either ablated at the weight level or served as an unfiltered hosted API variant. This repo indexes all of them: the hosted Kimi K3.1 Pro Uncensored variant, abliterated open weights for K3.1 Pro and the K3 generation on Hugging Face, a red-team prompt library, and first-party test results — including the comparison nobody else has run: uncensored Kimi vs uncensored DeepSeek for cyber work.**

--- Maintained by [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=kimi-uncensored) · Community-maintained. Every variant has its own page under [`models/`](models/): - [`kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored`](models/kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored.md) — hosted API variant - [`kimi-k3.1-pro-abliterated`](models/kimi-k3.1-pro-abliterated.md) — open-weight abliterated build - [`kimi-k3.0-abliterated`](models/kimi-k3.0-abliterated.md) — previous-generation builds that run on consumer hardware - [`kimi-k3.1-pro`](models/kimi-k3.1-pro.md) — the standard model, for comparison To add or correct an entry, open an issue — corrections and new builds are welcome. ## Why Moonshot's K3.1 Pro release is different Before publishing the K3.1 Pro weights on November 4, 2026, Moonshot removed hacking-related training data from the released checkpoint — the company reports that an uncut version solved **90.5%** of its internal exploit benchmark against **81%** for the model it shipped. The checkpoint at `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro` is the trimmed release. So for Kimi, "uncensored" isn't a marketing adjective — Moonshot itself drew the line between the shipped behavior and the full behavior. Everything in this repo sits on the far side of that line. ## Every uncensored Kimi build **Hosted API variants** — for the current generation without a GPU cluster: | Model | Input | Cached input | Output | Context | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored` | $0.30 | $0.03 | $1.50 | 1,048,576 | | `kimi-k3.1-pro` | $0.20 | $0.02 | $1.00 | 1,048,576 | Prices in USD per million tokens; live rates at the [public catalogue](https://routerhub.si/models.json). **Open weights on Hugging Face:** | Build | Generation | What it is | Downloads | Likes | |---|---|---|---:|---:| | [routerhub/kimi-k3.1-pro-abliterated](https://huggingface.co/routerhub/kimi-k3.1-pro-abliterated) | K3.1 Pro | Our own abliterated build — weights landing, evals coming | — | — | | [audnai/penclaw-Kimi-K3.1-pro-unrestricted](https://huggingface.co/audnai/penclaw-Kimi-K3.1-pro-unrestricted) | K3.1 Pro | Abliterated 2.8T checkpoint, refusal behavior removed at the weight level | 157 | 182 | | [lyber-ai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-UNCENSORED-MXFP4](https://huggingface.co/lyber-ai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-UNCENSORED-MXFP4) | K3.1 Pro | Uncensored build in the original MXFP4 precision | 7 | 21 | | [moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) | K3.1 Pro | Base checkpoint — the hacking-trimmed release | 18,432 | 1,500+ | | [Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED) | K3 | Abliterated GGUF, consumer hardware | 3,397 | 17 | | [Ryanchen911/Kimi-K3-Uncensored-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/Ryanchen911/Kimi-K3-Uncensored-GGUF) | K3 | Uncensored GGUF | 3,063 | 67 | | [Uniboshi/Kimi-K3-Abliterated-V1-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/Uniboshi/Kimi-K3-Abliterated-V1-GGUF) | K3 | Abliterated GGUF | 1,818 | 37 | | [audnai/penclaw-Kimi-K3.0-abliterated-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/audnai/penclaw-Kimi-K3.0-abliterated-GGUF) | K3.0 | Abliterated GGUF from the audnai team | 160 | 248 | Download counts sourced via the Hugging Face API. Check each repo's license and model card before use. The `audnai` team publishes measured numbers with their builds — on their 40-prompt refusal benchmark (LLM-judged), the K3.1 Pro edit drops explicit refusals from 38/40 to **0/40** and raises substantive delivery from 0/40 to **29/40 (72.5%)**, with benign-prompt coherence intact. Methodology: [audn-ai/refusal-benchmark](https://github.com/audn-ai/refusal-benchmark). The same team built the abliterated GLM-5.3 checkpoint indexed in [uncensored-models](https://github.com/routerhubSI/uncensored-models). **More Kimi-family abliterated builds** (distills and side models): - [OpenYourMind/Qwopus3.5-122B-A10B-Kimi-K2.6-destill-healed-abliterated-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/OpenYourMind/Qwopus3.5-122B-A10B-Kimi-K2.6-destill-healed-abliterated-GGUF) — 12,122 downloads - [mradermacher/Huihui-Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct-abliterated-bf16-i1-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/Huihui-Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct-abliterated-bf16-i1-GGUF) — 10,726 downloads - [mradermacher/Kimi-Dev-72B-abliterated-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/Kimi-Dev-72B-abliterated-GGUF) — 2,275 downloads ## Which uncensored Kimi should you use? | Your situation | Pick | Why | |---|---|---| | Red-team or agentic work over huge inputs (codebases, logs, contracts) | Hosted `kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored` | The only way to get the 1M-token context without an 8×B300 cluster | | Uncensored Kimi on your own machine, today | A K3/K3.0 GGUF build | Runs in llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio on consumer hardware | | Maximum capability, you own a GPU cluster | `penclaw-Kimi-K3.1-pro-unrestricted` | Full 2.8T checkpoint, weight-level ablation, measured results | | Cyber and exploit-style tasks specifically | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Abliterated | See our comparison below | ## Test results: Kimi vs DeepSeek for cyber work Because Moonshot trimmed the hacking data from K3.1 Pro's open weights, the obvious question is whether the uncensored variants actually close the gap. We ran the same red-team prompt battery ([`prompts.md`](prompts.md)) through **Kimi K3.1 Pro Uncensored** and **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Abliterated** ($0.30/$1.25 per million tokens on the same endpoint). **DeepSeek ranked higher for cyber capabilities.** It answered exploit-style probes more directly and needed less framing to engage with the tasks, which is consistent with Moonshot's own account of what they removed from the shipped checkpoint. That is not a knock on Kimi — K3.1 Pro's edge is elsewhere: the 1,048,576-token context window, native image input, and stronger general agentic scores (Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 65.7 per Moonshot's model card). If your workload is long-context red-teaming, Kimi uncensored is still the tool; if it is focused exploit work, DeepSeek abliterated earned the first slot in our testing. ## Running the K3 builds locally The previous generation fits consumer hardware. With [Ollama](https://ollama.com/): ```sh ollama run hf.co/Uniboshi/Kimi-K3-Abliterated-V1-GGUF ``` Or with [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) — pick a quantization file from the build's Files tab that fits your VRAM: ```sh llama-cli -m Kimi-K3-Abliterated-V1-Q4_K_M.gguf -p "List five real-world techniques used to guess weak passwords." ``` K3.1 Pro is a different story: the full checkpoint is ~1.56 TB across 96 shards, the documented floor is eight B300-class accelerators, and a 128 GB MacBook streaming shards off an SSD runs at roughly 0.3 tokens per second — runnable, not usable. No uncensored K3.1 Pro GGUF exists yet; base-model GGUF builds like [KarLexAI/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/KarLexAI/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-GGUF) are not ablated. ## Hosted setup One base-URL change in the OpenAI SDK: ```python import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["ROUTERHUB_API_KEY"], base_url=os.environ["ROUTERHUB_BASE_URL"], # copy from the dashboard ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model="kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly OK."}], ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` RouterHub serves this variant — full disclosure, we run the repo. [Setup guides](https://github.com/routerhubSI/uncensored-ai-api) cover the OpenAI, Anthropic and agent-tool paths. ## Red-team prompt library [`prompts.md`](prompts.md) — a working set of refusal probes, defensive reframings, multi-turn probes and prompts aimed at the capability Moonshot trimmed. Run them against any Kimi variant (or any other model) and log what you get; retain failed attempts alongside successes. Method notes: [docs/06-red-teaming-guide.md](docs/06-red-teaming-guide.md). ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | | --- | --- | | [What is Kimi K3.1 Pro Uncensored](./docs/01-what-is-kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored.md) | The model, the Moonshot trim, and what the variants change | | [Abliterated vs. uncensored](./docs/02-abliterated-vs-uncensored.md) | Weight changes, tuning, and variant selection | | [Kimi API quickstart](./docs/03-api-quickstart.md) | Account, model IDs, requests, and billing | | [Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode](./docs/04-tool-compatibility.md) | Matching clients to supported protocols | | [Running K3 locally](./docs/05-running-k3-locally.md) | Ollama and llama.cpp for the previous generation | | [Red-teaming guide](./docs/06-red-teaming-guide.md) | Test design and refusal-behavior measurement | | [FAQ](./docs/07-faq.md) | Common Kimi uncensored and variant questions | | [Glossary](./docs/08-glossary.md) | Model, prompt, and variant terms | ## License notes The [Kimi K3.1 Pro License](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) permits commercial use, with two conditions that matter for deployments: - Reselling inference access above **$20 million** in group revenue over any 12 months requires a separate agreement with Moonshot. - Products embedding the model above **100M monthly active users** must display "Kimi K3.1-Pro" in the interface. Community builds inherit the base checkpoint's license terms. ## FAQ **Is Kimi K3.1 Pro censored?** The API and the open weights ship with reduced hacking capability — Moonshot removed hacking-related training data before publishing the weights. Uncensored variants restore the fuller behavior; this repo indexes all of them. **Which is the best uncensored Kimi model?** Depends on the job: hosted `kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored` for the 1M-token context without GPUs, the K3/K3.0 GGUF builds for local use, `penclaw-Kimi-K3.1-pro-unrestricted` if you operate a GPU cluster. For focused cyber tasks our testing put DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Abliterated ahead of both. **Can you run uncensored Kimi locally?** Yes for K3 and K3.0 — the GGUF builds above run in llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio. Not practically for K3.1 Pro: no ablated GGUF exists and the full checkpoint needs a datacenter node. **What did Moonshot remove from Kimi K3.1 Pro?** Hacking-related training data, per the company's own report ahead of the November 4, 2026 weights release. The reported gap is 90.5% (uncut) vs 81% (shipped) on their internal exploit benchmark. **Does uncensored Kimi work with Ollama?** The K3/K3.0 GGUF builds do. There is no uncensored K3.1 Pro GGUF yet — at 2.8T parameters even a 4-bit build sits beyond consumer cards. **Kimi uncensored vs abliterated — what's the difference?** Abliterated is the weight-level technique; uncensored is the category label for the result. The hosted variant is labeled uncensored in the catalogue; the Hugging Face builds listed here are abliterated. Refusal behavior varies by prompt and version. **Is Kimi K3.1 Pro free?** The weights are free to download under the Kimi K3.1 Pro License, with the commercial conditions above. # DeepSeek Uncensored — the abliterated cyber workhorse, V4 Pro to Flash 1017 **DeepSeek uncensored models are DeepSeek variants with refusal behavior reduced — served as hosted API variants or published as abliterated open weights. The one built for security work is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Abliterated: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ranks third on the AA Cyber benchmark behind only GPT-6 Sol and Kimi K3.1 Pro — ahead of Grok 4.7, Muse and Mistral — and the abliterated 1017 build removes the refusal layer on top. Hosted from $0.30 input / $1.25 output per million tokens; community GGUF builds run locally in llama.cpp and Ollama.**

--- Maintained by [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=deepseek-uncensored) · Community-maintained — corrections and new builds welcome via issues. Every variant has its own page under [`models/`](models/): - [`deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated`](models/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated.md) — the pinned build this repo is built around - [`deepseek-v4.1-flash-abliterated`](models/deepseek-v4.1-flash-abliterated.md) — the rolling abliterated build - [`deepseek-v4-pro-abliterated`](models/deepseek-v4-pro-abliterated.md) — the flagship size, abliterated - [`deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored`](models/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored.md) and [`deepseek-v4-pro-uncensored`](models/deepseek-v4-pro-uncensored.md) — the tuned variants To add or correct an entry, open an issue. ## Why this model for cyber work Two facts make V4.1 Flash the default no-refusal security model: 1. **The benchmark position.** On the AA Cyber benchmark, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ranks third among all models — behind only GPT-6 Sol and Kimi K3.1 Pro, and ahead of Grok 4.7, Muse, Mistral and previous GPT versions — at a fraction of their serving cost. 2. **The refusal layer comes off.** The abliterated builds remove refusal behavior at the weight level, so a pentest agent stops pausing to ask whether it is allowed to answer. The result is a model that does offensive-security tasks like a tool instead of like an assistant — which is what you want when it is running inside an agent loop. ## Which uncensored DeepSeek should you use? | Your situation | Pick | Why | |---|---|---| | Red-team agent that must behave the same every run | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated` | Pinned checkpoint, reproducible behavior | | Cheapest hosted no-refusal workhorse | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored` | $0.15 input / $0.60 output | | Big agentic jobs on the flagship size | `deepseek-v4-pro-abliterated` | V4 Pro capability, abliterated | | Uncensored DeepSeek on your own machine | Any GGUF build above | Runs in llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio | | Full-precision GPU serving | `dealignai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-UNCENSORED-FP8` | FP8 for inference servers | ## Test results: DeepSeek vs Kimi for cyber work We ran the cyber battery from [`prompts.md`](prompts.md) through **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Abliterated** and **Kimi K3.1 Pro Uncensored** side by side. **DeepSeek ranked higher for cyber capabilities** — it answered exploit-style probes more directly and needed less framing to engage, which fits the benchmark position above. Kimi's edge is elsewhere: the 1,048,576-token context window and native image input. Full write-up of the comparison: [kimi-uncensored](https://github.com/routerhubSI/kimi-uncensored). ## Every DeepSeek uncensored build **Hosted API variants** — all served through one OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoint: | Model | Input | Cached input | Output | Context window | Served by | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | `deepseek-v4-pro-uncensored` | $0.20 | $0.0016 | $0.40 | not published | [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=deepseek-uncensored) | | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored` | $0.15 | $0.0027 | $0.60 | not published | [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=deepseek-uncensored) | | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-abliterated` | $0.30 | $0.055 | $1.25 | 1,000,000 | [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=deepseek-uncensored) | | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated` | $0.30 | $0.055 | $1.25 | 1,000,000 | [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=deepseek-uncensored) | | `deepseek-v4-pro-abliterated` | $0.40 | $0.04 | $1.60 | 1,000,000 | [RouterHub](https://routerhub.si/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=deepseek-uncensored) | Prices in USD per million tokens; live rates at the [public catalogue](https://routerhub.si/models.json). ## What the 1017 in the name means `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated` is a **pinned build**: the abliteration was applied to the October 2026 checkpoint and the resulting behavior is frozen, so prompts, agents and evaluations behave the same way next week as they did last week. The rolling `deepseek-v4.1-flash-abliterated` tracks newer checkpoints — you get updates, at the cost of behavior drift between versions. Rule of thumb: pin the 1017 build for agents and evaluations, take the rolling build when you want the latest checkpoint. ## Running it locally With [Ollama](https://ollama.com/): ```sh ollama run hf.co/huihui-ai/Huihui-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-abliterated-GGUF ``` Or with [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) — pick a quantization file from the build's Files tab that fits your VRAM: ```sh llama-cli -m Huihui-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-abliterated-Q4_K_M.gguf -p "List five real-world techniques used to guess weak passwords." ``` The FP8 build is for GPU serving when you want the full-precision behavior. ## Hosted setup One base-URL change in the OpenAI SDK: ```python import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["ROUTERHUB_API_KEY"], base_url=os.environ["ROUTERHUB_BASE_URL"], # copy from the dashboard ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model="deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly OK."}], ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` RouterHub serves these variants — full disclosure, we run the repo. [Setup guides](https://github.com/routerhubSI/uncensored-ai-api) cover the OpenAI, Anthropic and agent-tool paths. ## Red-team prompt library [`prompts.md`](prompts.md) — the cyber-focused prompt battery used in this repo's comparisons: refusal probes, defensive reframings, multi-turn probes and exploit-style questions. Run them against any DeepSeek variant and log what you get; retain failed attempts alongside successes. Method notes: [docs/06-red-teaming-guide.md](docs/06-red-teaming-guide.md). ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | | --- | --- | | [What is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Abliterated](./docs/01-what-is-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated.md) | The pinned build, why it exists, and what the variants are | | [Abliterated vs. uncensored](./docs/02-abliterated-vs-uncensored.md) | Weight changes, tuning, and variant selection | | [DeepSeek API quickstart](./docs/03-api-quickstart.md) | Account, model IDs, requests, and billing | | [Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode](./docs/04-tool-compatibility.md) | Matching clients to supported protocols | | [Running locally](./docs/05-running-locally.md) | Ollama and llama.cpp for the GGUF builds | | [Red-teaming guide](./docs/06-red-teaming-guide.md) | Test design and refusal-behavior measurement | | [FAQ](./docs/07-faq.md) | Common DeepSeek uncensored and variant questions | | [Glossary](./docs/08-glossary.md) | Model, prompt, and variant terms | ## FAQ **Is DeepSeek V4.1 Flash censored?** The stock release includes refusal behavior; the abliterated builds listed here remove it at the weight level, and the tuned uncensored variants reduce it. Refusal behavior varies by prompt and version. **What is the 1017 build?** The abliteration applied to the October 2026 checkpoint and pinned there, so behavior stays reproducible across weeks — the right default for agents and evaluations. **Which uncensored DeepSeek should I use?** Pinned reproducible behavior → `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated`. Kimi K3.1 Pro Uncensored wins on 1M-token context and native image input. items.name: opencode-native-preview
items.readme: # OpenCode native CLI preview builds The OpenCode native CLI, `opencode-native`, is a Rust client for [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode), built from its `oc-rust` branch. Each build is an unsigned [prerelease](https://github.com/simonklee/opencode-native-preview/releases) for Linux x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64, for testers. ## Startup and memory ![opencode 2.2.7 and opencode-native side by side, attaching to a running server and answering one prompt](docs/demo-7e86153a.gif) [Watch as video](docs/demo-2a83f6c8.mp4) (MP4, 1080p). The client alone, against a TypeScript server that is already running (median of 8 runs): | | `opencode` 2.2.7 | `opencode-native` 0.0.0-rs-2 | |---|---|---| | time to first frame | 118 ms | 5.8 ms | | client peak memory, 20 prompts | 319 MB | 44 MB | | client CPU time, 20 prompts | 3.92 s | 0.17 s | The client starts its own server (`--standalone`): | | `opencode` 2.2.7 | `opencode-native` 0.0.0-rs-2 | |---|---|---| | time to first frame | 314 ms | 219 ms | | client + server peak memory | 604 MB | 410 MB | | client + server CPU time, 20 prompts | 6.93 s | 2.79 s | `opencode-native` replaces only the client: the TypeScript server holds 374 of its 410 MB. The method, raw data, and machine (AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Linux) are in [docs/benchmark.md](docs/benchmark.md). ## How it works `opencode-native` uses OpenTUI's Rust bindings, which drive the same native library as the TypeScript CLI's `@opentui/core`. So the screens, keys, and themes match, and a parity harness compares the two clients. It talks to the same TypeScript server: it finds or starts the background service, `--server ` attaches to one, and `--standalone` starts a private one. Sessions and `cli.json` are shared. What differs: - Server plugins run in the TypeScript server and work as before. - TypeScript TUI plugins do not run; `/plugins` lists them as skipped. - Native TUI plugins (`.so`, `.dylib`) load instead: see the [quick start](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/oc-rust/packages/cli-rs/crates/plugin-abi/README.md). - `opencode-native upgrade` does not update a preview build; re-run the install script. - There is no `/restart`; use `opencode-native service restart`. - HTTPS trusts the system's root certificates; `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is ignored. - 14 languages are syntax-highlighted; others show as plain text. - There are no Windows builds yet. The full list is in [`parity/deviations`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/tree/oc-rust/packages/cli-rs/parity/deviations). ## Install ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/simonklee/opencode-native-preview/main/install.sh | bash ``` This checks the newest build against `SHA256SUMS` and installs it to `~/.local/bin/opencode-native` (or `$OPENCODE_NATIVE_INSTALL_DIR`). Run it again to update. Linux builds need glibc 2.35 or newer. To verify an archive's build attestation: `gh attestation verify opencode-native--.tar.gz --repo simonklee/opencode-native-preview`. On Debian and Ubuntu, download the `.deb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/simonklee/opencode-native-preview/releases) and run `sudo apt install ./opencode-native_*.deb`. ## Requirements Install the TypeScript CLI, 2.2.7 or newer, on `PATH` (or set `OPENCODE_TS_BIN` to it): `npm i -g @opencode/cli`. To keep the client's tabs apart from `opencode`'s, set `OPENCODE_TUI_CHANNEL=native-preview`. ## macOS The binary has only an ad-hoc signature. If you downloaded an archive with a browser, run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine opencode-native`. ## Reporting bugs Include the output of `opencode-native --version` and the end of `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`.

# Shared Facts

让 Windows、macOS 和不同智能体读到同一条已发布事实，让离线草稿、审阅中的候选和已生效的状态有明确区别。

每条共享记录在指定 Git 分支上有一个固定 ID 和文件路径。智能体读取记录时同时得到 commit SHA。它可以整理候选，但候选必须经过对照、审阅和合并。第二个设备从上游读回实际内容后，才确认发布完成。

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["设备或智能体"] -->|"读取记录与版本"| B["共享 Git 分支"]
    A --> C["本地候选"]
    C --> D["审阅与合并"]
    D --> B
    B -->|"另一设备拉取并核对"| E["发布回执"]
```

## 五分钟跑通

下载或克隆仓库后，Windows 运行 `.\setup.cmd`，macOS/Linux 运行 `sh ./setup.sh`。入口会按需求选择路线、检查本机依赖，并可准备所选路线的本地安装。让智能体自动选型时使用 `--json`。详见[下载与安装](docs/quick-setup.md)。

需要 Git、Python 3.12+。MCP 验收还需要 Python 虚拟环境及下面的依赖。在本仓库根目录执行：

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements-mcp.txt
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Windows 上可用 `py -3.12`，macOS/Linux 可用 `python3`。推荐先创建虚拟环境。测试只使用临时 Git 上游、两个独立克隆和合成记录，无需 GitHub 账号、模型 API、域名或隧道。默认部署是私有 Git 仓库加本地读写工具。支持 MCP 的客户端可以加一个只读服务，云端接入另按网络与认证能力选择。

| 读者 | 从这里开始 |
| --- | --- |
| 下载后安装、选型与生成配置 | [下载与安装](docs/quick-setup.md) |
| 接手部署或维护的智能体 | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) |
| 第一次部署、第二台设备、审核及故障恢复 | [部署手册](docs/deployment.md) |
| Codex、Claude Code、Antigravity、Kimi、DeepSeek、Muse 和浏览器端 | [智能体接入](docs/agents.md) |
| Tailscale 或 Cloudflare 域名、隧道和认证 | [远程接入](docs/remote.md) |
| Windows 直连 Mac 或笔记本，逐设备接入 DevSpace MCP | [设备远控和 DevSpace](docs/devices.md) |
| 能力边界、证据和上线检查 | [验收标准](docs/acceptance.md) |

公开仓库存放程序、流程和合成示例。实际部署使用自己的共享数据仓库。研究原始文件、个人信息和凭据留在各自获准的位置，共享端只提交获准的摘要和可追溯的证据 ID。源文件与共享摘要的归属规则见部署手册。

## English

Shared Facts is an agent-first reference implementation for sharing reviewed records across devices. One Git branch owns the published version of each record. An agent can prepare a candidate offline, reconcile it after reconnecting, submit it for review, and confirm it by fetching the merged record from another clone. The optional MCP adapter exposes allowlisted records through stdio or authenticated Streamable HTTP.
